notes:
Account snapshot: CodeFlow Prism builds an IDE-integrated PR assistant aimed at GitHub-style workflows. Main asks: near-real-time diff summarization, auto comment generation (per-team linting style), reranking of suggested comments, and low-latency streaming to the editor (WebSocket/GRPC).

Key context and timeline:
- 2026-02-10: Intro call (AE Maya + SE Ravi). High-level product fit — team of ~120 engs, high velocity, want to reduce PR review time by ~30%.
- 2026-02-18: Demo with product team (ff-20260218-PR-review-demo). Showed prototype using hosted LLMs; customer concerned about IP & repo residency.
- 2026-02-25: Security review kickoff — provided SOC2 + SOC2 roadmap, SSO/SAML integration details. Asked for KMS/HSM options and audit log retention policy.
- 2026-03-02: Deep-dive with infra and platform (ff-20260302-sync-call). SE asked about latency SLOs: target 50-150ms for single-line comment suggestions, 200-500ms for full diff summaries for 500-1k LOC diffs. Also discussed streaming chunked summaries for large diffs.
- 2026-03-03: POC scoping: 2-week POC, evaluate hosted API first, fallback to Dedicated for throughput and Private for repo-sensitive customers. POC metrics: latency, tokens per PR, cost per 1k reviews, comment relevance (team-labeled).

Technical and procurement notes:
- Preferred model configuration: small-medium sized open model with pinned versioning, option to fall back to quantized variants; want clear model/version pinning and rollout controls (canary A/B).
- Routing: regional routing important (NA primary, EU for EU repos), automatic fallback to cheaper model when load spikes.
- Caching: keen on prefix/KV caching for repeated review patterns; Redwood Optimize recommendations desired for batching and quantization.
- IDE integration: need streaming via WebSocket for editor plugin, token-level cost visibility for each PR, and tooling to suppress hallucinated suggestions.

POC milestones and immediate next actions:
- Deliver Dedicated perf matrix for mpt-7b / redwood-optimized variants by 2026-03-10 (blocker: bench infra answers).
- Send completed security questionnaire and KMS design doc link (Drive) — customer legal expects by 2026-03-12.
- Run 48-hour spike test: 500 real PRs through hosted API to measure median/95th latency and cost delta vs internal baseline. If pass -> move to dedicated sizing.

Customer quotes / snippets from calls:
- "We want suggestions that don't break style. If it's noisy, engineers will turn it off."
- "Pinning model versions is non-negotiable for us — unpredictable semantics across versions breaks CI."

Misc quick notes (shorthand):
- competitive: evaluated GitHub Copilot and Sourcegraph — Copilot good for dev productivity but lacks PR-level reranking and rerank-by-relevance features they want.
- pricing sensitivity: willing to commit to mid-sized ARR if SLA + residency + KMS satisfied.
- legal: retention controls required for EU repos.

Next meeting: POC kickoff with infra + security on 2026-03-09. Owner to circulate POC checklist and acceptance criteria.
